subject: PO metadata requirements, net terms and invoice cadence for Clearwell
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <procurement@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PO metadata requirements, net terms and invoice cadence for Clearwell

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. A couple quick items we need to lock down to finalize pricing and the discount eligibility for Clearwell's pilot:

1) PO fields: we need a persistent PO identifier, a business-unit code (BU), and remit address on every PO. In practice our billing engine uses the PO identifier + BU for invoice routing and discount calculation.

2) Net terms: our standard is net45. We can accept net60 for enterprise procurement but that changes discount eligibility (see below).

3) Invoice cadence: is Clearwell able to receive monthly invoices or do you require weekly/biweekly lanes? We can support multiple invoice lanes but discounts are tied to a single consolidated monthly statement.

Attached: SOW-Redwood-Standard-2027.pdf (standard SOW template)

Concrete ask from our side: can you send a sample PO (or your template) showing the BU and remittance fields you will populate? If you can confirm monthly invoicing and whether net60 is required, we’ll draft a slightly updated commercial term to reflect the invoicing cadence.

I copied Vanessa and Ben to coordinate the pricing fallback if Clearwell needs net60.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwellhealth.com
Date: 2027-09-14T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO metadata requirements, net terms and invoice cadence for Clearwell

Jordan —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from procurement side:

• Clearwell requires a PO number, BU code, billing entity, and remittance address on every purchase order. Our ERP will block invoices that are missing any of those fields.
• Standard payment term for our hospital group is net60. We prefer one consolidated invoice per month for each legal entity (monthly statement). We can do weekly billing for operational reasons but prefer monthly from an AP perspective.
• Regarding discounts: procurement needs clarity on what conditions trigger the 15% pilot discount you referenced. Is the discount applied per-invoice or per-monthly-statement?

I attached our PO template so you can see the fields we populate. If there’s anything that will cause invoices to be rejected by our ERP, we need to catch that before go-live.

Thanks —
Marta Ruiz
VP, Strategic Sourcing
Clearwell Health
Clearwell_PO_template_2027.docx (attached)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO metadata requirements, net terms and invoice cadence for Clearwell

Marta —

Thanks for the template, very helpful. Quick responses inline: 

• PO/ERP blocking: understood — our billing ops can map PO number, BU code, billing entity and remittance to your ERP fields. We’ll require PO number + BU to qualify invoices for the pilot discount. If the PO misses the BU code, invoices will still process but will be billed at standard list pricing.

• Net terms: we can accept net60. Two consequences: 1) pilot discount moves from 15% to 12% for net60, and 2) we require a pre-authorization (PO-level flag) that ties invoices to an approved monthly statement so we can consolidate and avoid duplicate credits.

• Invoice cadence: our preference is one consolidated monthly statement per legal entity. If you require weekly lanes for operational visibility, we can generate weekly invoices but the discount will only apply if you elect consolidated monthly settlement in writing.

Action: Vanessa/Ben — can we draft a short addendum that (a) records net60 with the adjusted 12% pilot discount and (b) includes the PO metadata mapping instructions for Clearwell's ERP? I’ll include a HubSpot note linking the PO template.

—Jordan

On a side note, quoting example added for clarity: 
> On Mon, Sep 14, 2027 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake wrote:
> > We need PO identifier + BU for discounting.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: PO mapping and pricing tradeoff proposal for Clearwell

Jordan / Ben — quick note on negotiation posture:

Proposal to present to Clearwell:
• Accept net60 but reduce the pilot discount from 15% -> 12% (this preserves cashflow expectations).
• Require BU code + PO id + billing entity on every invoice; if BU is absent, invoice processes at list price (no discount).
• Offer to support weekly invoice lanes for operational teams, but explicitly require electing consolidated monthly settlement to realize the 12% discount.

Risk notes: if Clearwell insists on weekly settlement with net60 we should require a prepayment reserve or escalate to finance for a credit hold. Also ask Legal to add a short clause that prevents duplicate credits when invoices are split across lanes.

If that looks good I’ll draft the addendum and a brief install guide for their AP team (field mappings + sample CSV).

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwellhealth.com
Date: 2027-09-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO metadata requirements, net terms and invoice cadence for Clearwell

Jordan/Vanessa —

Thanks for the clarity. Clearwell is willing to accept the net60/12% compromise if Redwood can:

1) Provide the one-page addendum that documents net60 and the 12% pilot discount tied to consolidated monthly statements;
2) Confirm Redwood billing will reject (or flag) invoices missing the BU code so our AP team can avoid rework; and
3) Accept our PO template as the source of truth for field names — if you need a field rename mapping, send it and we’ll review.

Please send the addendum draft and the mapping CSV and we’ll route for signatures. We’ll also replace the PO number in the attached template with a live PO once the addendum is in place.

Thanks —
Marta
VP, Strategic Sourcing
Clearwell Health
